sentences.text: In this appeal, the petitioners have challenged the judgment and award dated 21.11.2015 passed by the Additional Senior Civil Judge, M.A.C.T., Srirangapatna ('the Tribunal' for short) in M.V.C.No.1787/2012.

entities.text: Additional Senior Civil Judge, M.A.C.T., Srirangapatna
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, on 31.03.2012 at about 8.00 p.m., the husband of petitioner No.1,
father of petitioner No.2 by name Musthafa Khan, the deceased, while waiting for the bus at Pump House Circle, Srirangapatna Taluk, a KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-09/F-4555 knocked him down injuring on his left leg.
He was treated at K.R.Hospital as inpatient and his left leg was amputated below knee.
The deceased after taking treatment seeking compensation has approached the Tribunal.
Claim was opposed by the KSRTC.
When the claim petition NC: 2023:KHC:40774 was pending for consideration, on 23.02.2013, the deceased succumbed to death.
Hence, the petitioners were brought in as legal representatives of the deceased, who later amended the claim for compensation on account of death of the deceased.
The Tribunal after taking evidence, by impugned judgment dismissed the claim petition as not maintainable.
Aggrieved by the same, the petitioners have filed this appeal on various grounds.

4. Heard Smt.B.L.Asha, learned learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri.F.S.Dabali, learned counsel for respondent/KSRTC.
5.

It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that the deceased having suffered injury on account of accident caused by the KSRTC bus resulting in hospitalization, amputation of left leg below knee, huge money was spent towards treatment and also for the incidental expenses.
The dismissal of the claim petition only on the ground that NC: 2023:KHC:40774 the nexus between the death and accident is not established, is erroneous and sought for interference.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the KSRTC has contended that the accident was on 31.03.2012 and the deceased died on 23.02.2013, almost after 11 months of the accident.

There is no scope for amputated leg resulting in death, the petitioners have not produced any medical evidence to show that the deceased was under continuous treatment nor the death was reported to the Police nor the deceased was subjected to Postmortem examination to explain the cause of death.
The Police have charge sheeted the driver for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 338 of IPC read with Section 187 of IMV Act only.
The Tribunal is right in recording its finding that the death was not due to accidental injuries and the claim is not maintainable.

sentences.text: I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on both sides and also perused the materials on record.
8. There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of accident and injuries sustained by deceased.

The evidence on record did point out that the deceased was under hospitalization at K.R.Hospital,
Mysore, Vikram Hospital, Mysore and Vidyaranya Hospital, Mysore and the wheel of the bus ran over the left leg resulting in amputation of leg below knee.

The petitioners have spent Rs.90,126/-
towards treatment apart from the incidental expenses.
The deceased was under hospitalization for almost 17 days at 3 different dates between 31.03.2012 to 1.5.2012.
As the treatment could not save his left leg, it was amputated below knee.
If the deceased was alive, he is entitled to claim compensation on various heads.
Unfortunately he died on 23.02.2013.
The death was not reported to the Police nor there is any material on NC: 2023:KHC:40774 record to show that on account of amputation of leg, the death of deceased has occurred.
9. On record we have the evidence of petitioner No.1 as PW-1.
She has clearly stated that after amputation, except pain and suffering, treatment was not failed.
She also admitted that there was any occasion that the amputated leg to be infected nor the deceased was hospitalized post-amputation.
CW- 1/Dr.B.H. Manjunath is examined before the Court.
His evidence clearly points out that there was no post-operative infection suffered by the deceased, there is no chance of a person succumbed to death on account of amputation.
Unless he sees the Postmortem report, he may not be able to opine about cause of death.
From the medical evidence, it is thus clear that the death of deceased was not on account of amputation of left leg.
Hence, the Tribunal has rightly observed that when the cause of death is NC: 2023:KHC:40774 not proved, petitioners are not entitled to claim compensation and the petition is not maintainable.
10. I have carefully perused the impugned judgment.

While dismissing the claim petition, the Tribunal has observed that there was an accident, resulting in injuries to the deceased,
hospitalization, treatment and money spent towards treatment by the petitioners.
The claim was filed by the deceased himself as injured and the petitioners have come on record as his legal representatives later.
The petitioners may not be entitled to claim compensation for loss of dependency, but they are entitled to be reimbursed for the money that they have spent towards treatment of the deceased.
The deceased suffered amputation, medical bills itself comes to Rs.90,126/-.
He was under hospitalization for 17 days.

He has suffered post-operative pain and sufferings, an attendant attended him for considerable period and he and his family members NC:
2023:KHC:40774 suffered loss of income during laid up period.

The money that has been spent by the petitioners would have been saved as the estate and therefore, the petitioners are entitled to claim reimbursement of the medical and incidental expenses that they have spent towards treatment of the deceased.
11. As observed above, the medical bills itself comes to Rs.90,126/-.

Taking into consideration 17 days of hospitalization on three occasions, money spent towards transportation, food and nourishment, attendant and also other incidental expenses, it may come around Rs.35,000/-
together.
Hence, the Tribunal ought to have taken cognizance of these aspects and awarded compensation under these heads.

(iv) Rest of the judgment and award of the Tribunal is kept intact.
